summary: Weekly POC check-in to gate Redwood performance vs incumbent. Redwood shows materially lower median latency and higher sustained throughput in controlled runs, but tail p95 spikes persist in cold-cache and long-sequence scenarios. Discussion focused on routing thresholds, KV prefix cache warming, quantization impact on quality, dedicated slot sizing, and security documentation. Agreed next steps: locked head-to-head, cost sheet, and security deep-dive.
topics: Median and tail latency comparisons vs baseline provider
Routing/fallback policy and hysteresis to avoid flapping
Dedicated slot sizing and cost delta
transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2027-01-12
Start: 11:00 AM PST
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Carlos Ruiz (Havenwell - Head of ML), Farah Singh (Havenwell CTO), Evan Lee (Havenwell Infra)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood. Quick agenda — we'll walk the bench numbers, routing options and decisions on canary vs direct cutover.
[00:28] Carlos Ruiz: Hey Maya, yeah thanks. We ran the 50k sample overnight, saw some interesting differences, um, p50 looks great but p95 still a bit... spiky.
[01:03] Liam O'Neill: Right, so to call out the numbers we saw median latency for Redwood-rt variant around 72ms p50 whereas the incumbent was about 118-125ms p50 on the same token length distribution.
[01:35] Farah Singh: Wait you said 72? That seems almost half, ok that's good. What about throughput? Our baseline does 900 rps sustained at 10 token window.
[02:02] Liam O'Neill: We were seeing steady 1.2k rps on the dedicated slot config, with sustained bursts to 1.5k before queueing increased. Unit-cost wise, with quantize-8 profile we're below baseline by ~18% token cost.
[02:41] Evan Lee: Is that with KV cache enabled? We noticed when KV cache was off our tail got worse.
[03:10] Liam O'Neill: Good call — the numbers I quoted include the KV prefix cache in play. Without it p95 jumps to, uh, about 430-480ms in some runs, which is comparable to baseline. With prefix caching p95 dropped to 210-260ms.
[03:52] Carlos Ruiz: Hmm so cache is a big factor. But in production we have 30% cold starts — keys not present — so that delta will show up unless we warm the cache.
[04:18] Maya Chen: We discussed warming strategies in last week's notes; we can script a warm-up load or use proactive cache population at inference time. Also routing fallback to baseline for cold keys is an option.
[04:47] Farah Singh: About routing: we want a performance gate — if p95 goes over 300ms over 1 minute, fallback to baseline. Is that simple to implement?
[05:20] Liam O'Neill: Yes, we can surface a routing policy that checks latency and error rate; the SLO-based policy can be tuned. There's some nuance around in-flight requests and the KV cache state while failing over.
[05:55] Carlos Ruiz: Any quality regressions with quantize-8? Our NLU tests flagged a 0.8% BLEU-ish style drift on entity extraction.
[06:30] Liam O'Neill: We measured a tiny delta; most customers don't see user-facing degradations at quantize-8 but for critical entity extraction tasks we can run a small eval set. We'll paste detailed eval CSV.
[07:02] Evan Lee: Can you also share the profiler traces? We need to line up our infra traces with your traces to see queuing effects.
[07:34] Maya Chen: Yep we'll provide the trace bundle. Liam — also share the per-route cost breakdown.
[07:50] Liam O'Neill: Will do. Quick note: the p95 spikes we saw correlate with long-tail token sequences and cross-model fallbacks during some routing experiments.
[08:16] Carlos Ruiz: Could you repeat the head-to-head with the exact same seed and prompt set? We suspect the prompt distribution varied slightly in the overnight run.
[08:42] Liam O'Neill: Absolutely. We'll run a locked-run with identical seeds, same prompt queue and attach request ids so you can correlate.
[09:09] Farah Singh: On the dedicated slot sizing — what's your recommendation if we want 99.9% of requests under 300ms p95 at 1.2k rps?
[09:38] Liam O'Neill: For that target we'd recommend two dedicated slots with auto-burst pool of one; depends on model variant and quantization. With q8 we'd likely meet it; with q4 it's lower but quality risk.
[10:06] Evan Lee: Two slots plus burst — can you give cost delta vs baseline for monthly 24/7? We need CapEx/OpEx numbers.
[10:30] Maya Chen: We'll put that in the dedicated cost sheet. I'll include amortized GPU hours and expected unit cost.
[11:00] Carlos Ruiz: Back to routing thresholds — we want to avoid flapping. What hysteresis do you suggest?
[11:25] Liam O'Neill: Use a 90s window with rolling p95 and require two consecutive breaches to flip. That reduces flapping and gives time for caches to recover.
[11:50] Farah Singh: Makes sense. Ok for the canary A/B— how do we capture metrics to compare quality and latency side by side?
[12:12] Liam O'Neill: We'll tag requests and compute p50/p95, throughput, errors, and quality evals on sample subset. We'll also stream traces to your S3.
[12:40] Carlos Ruiz: Any known dependency on network egress in your hosted region that could bias latency vs our baseline which is in a different cloud region?
[13:05] Maya Chen: We put the pilot in the same region as your incumbent for fairness. Some minor network variance remains but we can localize by running both in same AZ.
[13:38] Evan Lee: About security and compliance — we need SOC2 docs and encryption details before we go to dedicated. Who owns that?
[14:02] Maya Chen: I'll connect you with our Security lead and drop SOC2, ISO artifacts and our KMS/HSM integration doc. Liam will join the session for technical Qs.
[14:26] Farah Singh: Great. Also, for audit logs we need token-level tracing for 90 days — is that feasible?
[14:45] Liam O'Neill: We can provide detailed logs; retention beyond standard will be an add-on but feasible.
[15:10] Carlos Ruiz: On the p95 spikes, could kernel selection or the compilation path be causing jitter?
[15:36] Liam O'Neill: Yes, in some edge cases kernel fallback happens for very long sequences; we're optimizing the kernel selector. We'll flag runs where it happened.
[15:58] Maya Chen: Ok let's get concrete next steps — do we agree Redwood will run the locked head-to-head and provide CSVs and cost estimates by Friday?
[16:16] Carlos Ruiz: Yes, and we'll provide production traces and our token distribution tomorrow.
[16:34] Farah Singh: Also schedule the security deep-dive for next Tuesday, 11am our time.
[16:50] Maya Chen: Noted. Liam — you have the routing playbook doc to share?
[17:05] Liam O'Neill: I'll share a draft after the call.
[17:20] Evan Lee: Quick Q — if we do fallback to baseline, do we preserve session KV state and prompt continuity?
[17:40] Liam O'Neill: Not automatically; we'd send a marker and rehydrate KV where possible. There's a brief continuity gap for in-flight sessions.
[18:05] Carlos Ruiz: Alright. For the A/B we also want to capture user-perceived latency from the front end to see end-to-end impact.
[18:24] Maya Chen: Good point, include your front-end metrics pipeline in the trace correlations.
[18:50] (small crosstalk)
[19:10] Liam O'Neill: I'll also enable longer tail logging for the next runs so we can inspect specific long-running requests.
[19:30] Carlos Ruiz: Perfect. Anything else on the bench numbers?
[19:52] (pause)
[20:05] Farah Singh: No, I think that's it. Recap please.
[20:20] Maya Chen: Recap — Redwood runs locked head-to-head, share per-run CSVs and trace bundle by Friday; routing playbook and dedicated cost estimate by Friday; security deep-dive next Tuesday; customer provides prod traces and token distribution by tomorrow. Action items in the doc. Thanks all.
[20:50] Call ends

Post-call Notes: We observed mixed-case transcription errors: 'KV cash' transcribed in one snippet; 'Redwood RT' transcribed as 'red wood art' in auto notes. Some speaker labels were generic in the AI transcription; manual QA applied but not full clean-up.

Action Items Recap:
- Maya Chen: Share routing playbook, dedicated cost estimate, SOC2 & KMS docs (due 2027-01-14)
- Liam O'Neill: Run locked head-to-head, enable prefix KV and extended logging, share profiler traces (due 2027-01-15)
- Evan Lee: Provide production QPS trace and token distribution (due 2027-01-13)
